title: SLO evidence and escalation runway — implementation plan
content:
Purpose
---
This is a cross-functional implementation plan to create a reliable, lightweight evidence collection and escalation runway for SLO breaches and near-breaches. Goal: reduce time-to-decision during incidents, improve signal fidelity for product owners, and standardize evidence bundles for postmortems and SLO reviews.

Scope
---
- Applies to production model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated pools).
- Focus on availability and latency SLOs for model inference endpoints (p99 latency, availability per route).
- Excludes offline eval/regression SLOs (handled by applied-ml).

Definitions (quick)
---
- Evidence bundle: compact collection of telemetry and contextual metadata used to evaluate an SLO event (logs, traces, metrics, request samples, rollout flags).
- Near-breach: 10–25% of error budget consumed in a rolling 1h window or p99 > threshold for two consecutive 5m windows.
- Breach: Error budget > 100% consumed over defined window or sustained p99 > threshold for 15 minutes per SLO policy.

Success criteria (what "done" looks like)
---
1. On-call can produce an evidence bundle within 10 minutes of being paged for a near-breach.
2. Product owners receive a clear escalation recommendation (no action / mitigation / rollback) within 20 minutes.
3. Automated evidence templates are attached to incidents and to SLO review tickets in Jira.
4. 90% of escalations contain the key 6 evidence artifacts (metric snapshot, traces, recent deploys, recent config changes, sample requests, error log snippet).

Owner & Role matrix (high level)
---
- SRE lead (owner): Alyssa Chen — program owner and single-threaded point for cross-team delivery.
- Observability (metrics/tracing): Marco Diaz — define dashboards, alert shape, template queries.
- Serving runtime engineering: Priya Nair — ensure traces include model version, quantization metadata, KV cache hits.
- Platform infra / deploys: Evan Brooks — surface deploy metadata in incidents; ensure release tags present.
- Product liaison: Lina Torres — decision authority for product-facing escalations; validates risk thresholds.

Instrumentation checklist (minimum required per route)
---
- Metric: request count, success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency by route and model-version-tagged.
- Traces: end-to-end spans with model.name and model.version; inference kernel duration and GPU queue time.
- Logs: sampled request logs (json) with request id, user id hash, route, model hash.
- Deploy metadata: release id, canary percentage, machine pool id.
- Feature flags: rollout flags and routing policy snapshot.
- KV/prefix cache hit ratio and recent TTL evictions.

Evidence bundle template (ordered)
---
1) Snapshot header: time window, SLO id, cumulative burn %, alert threshold hit time, owner contact.
2) Metric graphs (links) for the last 60m and last 24h (p99 and error_budget_burn).
3) Top 5 traces (linked) for high-latency/error requests with annotated span durations.
4) Last deploys table (last 3) with git SHA, env, rollout %, and responsible engineer.
5) Config delta: recent config changes (routing, batching, quantization profiles).
6) 3 sample request payloads (redacted) and responses demonstrating failure mode.
7) Recent autoscale / capacity events from Dedicated pools.
8) Short TL;DR: likely root cause hypothesis and recommended immediate step (rollback / throttle / safe-fallback model).

Alert triage flow (oncall)
---
- Pager triggers for near-breach (severity 2): oncall follows a 10-min checklist — collect snapshot, tag incident as "SLO-near-breach", notify product-laison.
- If evidence supports systemic degradation, escalate to severity 1 (page product and infra leads).
- Use the evidence bundle template to populate the incident ticket (link to SRE-342).

Escalation matrix (summary)
---
- Oncall -> SRE shift lead (15 min) -> Product owner (20 min) -> Exec on-call (30–45 min)
- Automatic escalation if error budget burn exceeds configured multiplier (e.g., 3x baseline for 10m).

Communications & runbook snippets
---
- Slack channel: #sre-incidents (used for real-time updates). Use the incident template deployable from PlaybookBot.
- Incident postmortem template includes the evidence bundle as an attachment.
- External comms (customer-facing) drafts are prepared by CS with product owner sign-off.

30/60/90 rollout plan (tactical)
---
- 0–30 days (triage + quick wins):
  - Implement the evidence bundle template in incident tool (attachable macro). (owner: Marco)
  - Add model.version tagging to traces and ensure request ids propagate. (owner: Priya)
  - Run two tabletop exercises with Product and Infra to validate escalation timings. (owner: Alyssa)
- 31–60 days (automation + instrumentation):
  - Auto-generate metric snapshot attachments for alerts (via telemetry-config). (owner: Marco + Evan)
  - Implement a small Lambda to collect top traces and redact sensitive fields automatically. (owner: Observability)
  - Pilot on two high-traffic routes (chat/generation). Collect feedback. (owner: SRE + Product)
- 61–90 days (scale + policy):
  - Formalize escalation SLAs and add to team contracts. (owner: Alyssa + Lina)
  - Integrate evidence bundles into monthly SLO reviews and runbook library. (owner: SRE)
  - Expand pilot to Dedicated clusters and private deployments. (owner: Platform)

Dependencies & risks
---
- Dependent on telemetry ingestion capacity: if cluster saturates we may miss traces. Mitigation: sampling rules and prioritized spans.
- Serving runtime must expose model metadata; risk if older models lack metadata tagging. Mitigation: compatibility shim in gateway.
- Cultural risk: product owners might be slow to adopt automated recommendations; mitigation: tabletop rehearsals and schedule 1:1s.

Workshops / meetings (proposed)
---
- Kickoff (week 0): 60m cross-functional overview + alignment on SLO thresholds.
- Instrumentation clinic (week 1–2): hands-on session for runtime and observability engineers.
- Tabletop #1 (week 3): simulated near-breach exercise.
- Post-pilot review (week 8): gather qualitative feedback and finalize SLA language.

Open questions (to resolve)
---
- What is the canonical threshold for "near-breach" across product routes? (proposed: 25% of hourly burn).
- Should evidence bundles be stored persistently for 90 days or attached only to incidents? (privacy + storage cost tradeoff).
- How granular should automated rollback rules be — route-level or model-variant-level?

Immediate next steps (this week)
---
- Marco: create evidence bundle incident macro and link to SRE-342.
- Priya: add model.version to one canary route and confirm trace availability.
- Alyssa: schedule kickoff and invite Product/Infra/Observability owners.

Notes to self / quick ideas (informal)
---
- Consider a lightweight "SLO smoke" job that runs a standard prompt set to measure tail latency every 5m. Could be useful as an external signal.
- Keep evidence bundle < 5MB when stored; otherwise store referenced links.
- Want a single button in the incident UI "collect evidence bundle now" that runs the Lambda.

References
---
- Confluence: SLO Evidence Framework (linked artifact).
- Jira: SRE-342 (implementation epic).
- GitHub telemetry-config PR 58 (adds snapshot endpoint).

If you're editing: please add short notes inline and tag @alyssa. This doc is the single-threaded plan for the next 90 days; iterate freely but keep the template stable.
